audit_findings.title: The completed Hexagon acquisition makes the numerator, bridge and denominator temporally incoherent
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.101008 billion purchase consideration, including $2.2 billion cash and 3.224 million shares valued at $902.208 million; 15.3% of the $20.292 billion base-case equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The June 2026 bridge and share denominator reflect the acquisition, while the 2025 owner-earnings anchor excludes the acquired operations.
audit_findings.evidence: Approximately € 810 million of the aggregate consideration will be paid in the form of newly issued shares of Cadence’s common stock, par value $0.01 per share.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing mismatch. The June balance sheet captures the cash expenditure, and the 275.393 million outstanding shares include the acquisition issuance; the 281.046 million valuation denominator is higher still. But the numerator remains pre-acquisition. Filed six-month pro forma results differ from reported results by $63.595 million of revenue and negative $13.641 million of net income, but these figures cover only the pre-closing stub and acquisition-accounting adjustments, not a normalized D&E owner-earnings run rate. Given the transaction's size relative to calculated equity value, the mismatch can materially change intrinsic value, principally upward once sustainable acquired earnings are included.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild owner earnings on a post-closing perimeter using D&E operating cash generation, maintenance capital and integration costs; reconcile the $2.2 billion cash payment, $154.6 million acquired cash, 3.224 million issued shares and preliminary assumed liabilities to the June balance sheet before rerunning all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The stated purge of portfolio income is not demonstrated and may double count cash
audit_findings.magnitude: The $1,195.7 million anchor is only $0.855 million above unadjusted net income plus depreciation and amortization less capital expenditure of $1,194.845 million; identified positive non-operating items total $184.702 million pre-tax
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-operating interest and investment returns appear to remain in owner earnings while cash and short-term investments are separately added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Other income, net consists primarily of interest earned on cash, cash equivalents and investments in debt securities, realized and unrealized gains and losses from our strategic investments in equity securities of other companies, gains and losses from investments held in the Nonqualified Deferred Compensation (“NQDC”) trust and foreign exchange gains and losses.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated workpaper inconsistency, although the exact tax-adjusted correction remains unresolved. The filed positive items are $101.584 million of interest income, $57.589 million of investment gains, $14.029 million of NQDC trust gains and an $11.5 million asset-sale gain. Their $184.702 million gross total equals 15.4% of the anchor. NQDC gains require matching against related compensation expense, and operating foreign-exchange effects should be retained, so the final correction cannot be inferred from the gross total alone. Nevertheless, the scale is sufficient to materially overstate value if these returns were capitalized and the associated assets were also added in the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Produce the anchor reconciliation and rerun after separately removing each non-operating item with its actual tax effect, matching NQDC income to NQDC compensation expense and retaining only demonstrably operating foreign-exchange effects.

audit_findings.title: Serial acquisition spending may be an uncharged maintenance cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.365463 billion of acquisition cash spending during 2023-2025, averaging $455.154 million annually; $105.332 million of acquired-intangible amortization was added back in 2025, but the maintenance portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Owner earnings add back acquired-intangible amortization without deducting any normalized cost of replacing acquired technology, customer relationships or capabilities.
audit_findings.evidence: Our strategy includes continuing to purchase intangible assets and acquiring other companies and businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved economic-classification issue, not a demonstrated error. Acquisition spending averaged 38.1% of the current owner-earnings anchor, while 2025 acquired-intangible amortization alone was 8.8% of the anchor. Those comparisons show potentially substantial exposure, but the record does not establish what portion of acquisition spending was necessary to maintain Cadence's competitive position rather than fund incremental growth. Materiality therefore remains uncertain.
audit_findings.action: Classify at least five to ten years of acquisitions by replacement versus expansion purpose, compare acquired-product attrition and technological obsolescence with organic R&D, and rerun using either a normalized maintenance-acquisition charge or no addback for amortization tied to assets requiring replenishment.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may omit required working-capital investment
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed operating-asset and liability movements produced computed net cash uses of $73.251 million in 2025, $208.975 million in 2024 and $98.778 million in 2023; three-year average $127.001 million, or 10.6% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Accrual earnings are capitalized without deducting recurring investment in receivables, contract assets, inventory and related operating balances.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025 and 2024, our cash flows from operating activities was impacted by growth in our System Design and Analysis business in which revenue is recognized at a point in time and cash is typically collected over the term of the arrangement.
audit_findings.explanation: The anchor's near-exact correspondence to net income plus depreciation and amortization less capital expenditure demonstrates that no working-capital charge was included. The filed cash-flow movements show recurring net uses despite offsets from payables and deferred revenue. The three-year average is large enough to materially affect owner earnings and value, although a normalized charge must exclude acquisition-related and genuinely transitory movements.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile receivables, unbilled receivables, contract assets, inventory, payables and deferred revenue over a full cycle; isolate acquisition and timing effects, then rerun all scenarios with the resulting normalized working-capital requirement.

audit_findings.title: A historical export-control penalty appears to remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $128.545 million, equal to 10.8% of the anchor; normalization would add approximately $2.017 billion or $7.18 per share to the base case before considering recurring compliance costs
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring charge reduced 2025 net income and therefore the owner-earnings anchor, while the anchor calculation contains no evident normalization adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: As part of the settlements, we recorded a charge of $128.5 million in Loss related to contingent liability on our consolidated income statement and paid BIS and the DOJ aggregate net penalties and forfeitures of $140.6 million during fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated anchor error if the stated objective is normalized owner earnings. The charge settled violations from 2015-2021 and was non-deductible, so its removal would add the full $128.545 million rather than a conventionally tax-affected amount. Its scale materially depresses calculated value. Continuing probation, audit, reporting and compliance expenditures are recurring operating costs and must remain; they cannot be removed with the penalty.
audit_findings.action: Trace the anchor ledger to confirm the charge is present, add back only the $128.545 million historical settlement charge, retain all ongoing compliance costs and rerun the three valuation scenarios.

audit_findings.title: An unfunded pension claim may be absent from the bridge
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded defined-benefit obligation not otherwise reflected would be a senior claim requiring deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The unfunded projected benefit obligation for Cadence’s defined benefit retirement plans is recorded in other long-term liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings establish that an unfunded projected benefit obligation exists and is recorded within other long-term liabilities, but they do not disclose its latest amount separately. The $10.837 million accumulated-other-comprehensive-loss component for defined-benefit plans is not the funded-status liability and cannot be used as its amount. Consequently, omission is possible, but the supplied record cannot establish whether the obligation is large enough to be material or whether part of it is already captured elsewhere.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest actuarial funded-status schedule showing projected benefit obligations, plan assets and tax effects, reconcile it to other long-term liabilities, and rerun the bridge with the net unfunded claim if it is not otherwise captured.
